places.name: Mumbai
see: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, a working station and a UNESCO site
Elephanta Caves by ferry from the Gateway of India
Marine Drive at dusk and the Art Deco buildings around the Oval Maidan
Kala Ghoda's galleries and the cafés of Colaba
places.tip: Vande Bharats leave from CSMT and Mumbai Central; local trains link the two.

places.name: Ahmedabad
see: The pols of the walled city, India's first UNESCO World Heritage City
Sabarmati Ashram, Gandhi's home from 1917 to 1930
Adalaj stepwell, 20 km north
Street food at Manek Chowk after dark
places.tip: Trains to Jodhpur leave from Sabarmati, 6 km from Ahmedabad Junction.

places.name: Jodhpur
see: Mehrangarh Fort above the blue old city
The marble cenotaphs of Jaswant Thada
Umaid Bhawan Palace museum
The clock tower market at Sardar Bazaar
places.tip: The morning train to Jaipur and Delhi leaves at 05:30.

places.name: Jaipur
see: Amber Fort, best reached early
City Palace and Jantar Mantar, a UNESCO-listed observatory
The facade of Hawa Mahal at sunrise
Nahargarh Fort for the view over the walled city
places.tip: The walled city is a UNESCO World Heritage City; Amber gets crowded by mid-morning.

places.name: Delhi
see: Humayun's Tomb and the Qutb Minar, both UNESCO sites
Red Fort and the lanes of Chandni Chowk
Lodhi Garden and the lawns around India Gate
The Crafts Museum and regional food at Dilli Haat
places.tip: Vande Bharats use five Delhi stations; allow an hour to cross the city. November smog and December fog are the worst months.

places.name: Katra
see: The 13 km climb to the Vaishno Devi shrine
The lit-up pilgrim path at night
Reasi and the Chenab bridge, the world's highest railway arch, nearby
places.tip: The Vaishno Devi trek takes most of a day; pilgrims must register for a yatra slip first.

places.name: Srinagar
see: A shikara on Dal Lake and a night on a houseboat
The Mughal gardens of Nishat, Shalimar and Chashme Shahi
The old city's Jamia Masjid and Khanqah of Shah-e-Hamadan
Day trips to Gulmarg, Sonamarg or Pahalgam
places.tip: The station is at Nowgam, about 10 km from Dal Lake. Winter brings snow and short days; the tulip garden opens in spring.

places.name: Amritsar
see: The Golden Temple at dawn and again at night
The langar, which feeds tens of thousands a day
The Jallianwala Bagh memorial
The Attari–Wagah border ceremony each evening
places.tip: The border ceremony is about 30 km away and starts before sunset; arrive early.

places.name: Agra
see: The Taj Mahal at sunrise
Agra Fort
Itmad-ud-Daulah's inlaid marble tomb
Fatehpur Sikri, 40 km west
places.tip: The Taj Mahal is closed on Fridays.

places.name: Varanasi
see: A boat past the ghats at dawn
The evening Ganga aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat
Sarnath, where the Buddha first taught, 10 km away
The old city's lanes and Banarasi silk weavers
places.tip: Trains use two stations, Varanasi Junction and Banaras, about 4 km apart.

places.name: Patna
see: Bihar Museum
Takht Sri Patna Sahib, birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh
The ruins of Nalanda Mahavihara, a UNESCO site, 90 km away
Rajgir's hills and the Vishwa Shanti Stupa
places.tip: Nalanda and Rajgir make a full day out by road.

places.name: New Jalpaiguri
see: Darjeeling, about three hours up by road
The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, a UNESCO site
Tea gardens around Kurseong
Mahananda Wildlife Sanctuary
places.tip: NJP, in Siliguri, is the gateway to Darjeeling, Sikkim and the Dooars.

places.name: Guwahati
see: Kamakhya Temple on Nilachal Hill
A sunset cruise on the Brahmaputra
Umananda temple on a river island
Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO site, about four hours east
places.tip: Kaziranga's safaris run from about November to April.

places.name: Kolkata
see: Victoria Memorial and the Maidan
Howrah Bridge and the flower market below it
Kumartuli, where the clay idols are made
Dakshineswar and Belur Math on the Hooghly
places.tip: Durga Puja in September or October is the city's biggest festival.

places.name: Puri
see: Jagannath Temple (only Hindus may enter)
The Sun Temple at Konark, a UNESCO site, 35 km away
Chilika Lake for dolphins and migratory birds
Raghurajpur, a village of pattachitra painters
places.tip: The Rath Yatra fills the town in June or July.

places.name: Tatanagar
see: Jubilee Park in Jamshedpur
Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary, known for its elephants
Dimna Lake below the Dalma hills
places.tip: Tatanagar is Jamshedpur's station, a useful overnight between Odisha and Bihar.

places.name: Gaya
see: The Mahabodhi Temple and the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya, a UNESCO site
Monasteries built by Buddhist countries
The Great Buddha Statue
Vishnupad Temple in Gaya town
places.tip: Bodh Gaya is 15 km from Gaya station; stay there.

places.name: Khajuraho
see: The Western Group of temples, a UNESCO site
The sound and light show at the temples
Panna National Park, 25 km away
Raneh Falls canyon
places.tip: The Khajuraho Dance Festival runs for a week in late February.

places.name: Orchha
see: Raja Mahal and Jahangir Mahal
The royal chhatris on the Betwa river
The evening aarti at Ram Raja Temple
The view from the roof of Chaturbhuj Temple
places.tip: Orchha has no Vande Bharat station; it is 16 km by road from Jhansi.

places.name: Gwalior
see: Gwalior Fort and Man Singh Palace
Teli ka Mandir and the Sas-Bahu temples
Jai Vilas Palace
Tansen's tomb
places.tip: The fort fits between a morning and an evening train.

places.name: Bhopal
see: The stupas of Sanchi, a UNESCO site, 46 km away
Bhimbetka rock shelters, a UNESCO site, 45 km away
The Upper Lake at sunset
Taj-ul-Masajid and the old city
places.tip: Trains use Bhopal Junction and Rani Kamlapati, about 6 km apart.

places.name: Nagpur
see: Deekshabhoomi, where B. R. Ambedkar became a Buddhist in 1956
Tadoba tiger reserve, reached through Chandrapur
Ambazari Lake
Sitabuldi Fort
places.tip: Tadoba's safaris book up early.

places.name: Hyderabad
see: Charminar and the Laad Bazaar bangle market
Golconda Fort and the Qutb Shahi tombs
Salar Jung Museum
Hyderabadi biryani
places.tip: Trains east and south leave from Secunderabad.

places.name: Chennai
see: Kapaleeshwarar Temple in Mylapore
Marina Beach and San Thome Basilica
Fort St George and the Government Museum
Mahabalipuram's shore temples, a UNESCO site, 55 km away
places.tip: Heavy north-east monsoon rain falls from October to early December; the music season follows in December.

places.name: Mysuru
see: Mysore Palace, lit up on Sunday evenings
Chamundi Hill and its Nandi
Srirangapatna's fort and Tipu Sultan's summer palace
Devaraja Market
places.tip: Dasara in September or October is the city's biggest celebration.

places.name: Bengaluru
see: Lalbagh and Cubbon Park
Bangalore Palace and Tipu Sultan's palace
The food streets of VV Puram
Nandi Hills at sunrise, 60 km north
places.tip: Vande Bharats use four city stations; KSR Bengaluru is the central one.

places.name: Kochi
see: The Chinese fishing nets of Fort Kochi
Mattancherry Palace and the Paradesi Synagogue
A Kathakali performance
The Kochi-Muziris Biennale, in the winters it runs
places.tip: Ernakulam Junction is on the mainland; take the ferry to Fort Kochi.

places.name: Alappuzha
see: Houseboats and canoes on the backwaters
Vembanad Lake
Alappuzha beach and lighthouse
Kumarakom's bird sanctuary across the lake
places.tip: Even a few hours by canoe through the canals is worth it.

places.name: Mangaluru
see: Panambur and Tannirbhavi beaches
Kadri Manjunath Temple
The painted walls of St Aloysius Chapel
Udupi's Krishna temple, an hour north
places.tip: Try kori rotti, neer dosa and the fish curries.

places.name: Goa
see: The churches of Old Goa, a UNESCO site
Fontainhas, the old Latin quarter of Panaji
Beaches from Palolem in the south to Morjim in the north
A spice plantation near Ponda
places.tip: Madgaon is in the south; Thivim is closer to the northern beaches.
